target_in_paper: Section 7.1, Problem 7.3 (Scheepers): "Does S1(Ω, T) imply Ufin(O, Γ)?" ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official symbolic formulation exactly and uses the intended properties and implication without broadening the problem. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
missing_details: It should explicitly quantify over a set of real numbers X, since the chapter restricts attention to sets of reals. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
O should be identified as the collection of open covers of X. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

The paper’s standing convention is that a cover is nontrivial, i.e. X itself is not a member of the cover. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

Ω should be defined as the family of open ω-covers of X: for every finite F⊆X, some U in the cover contains F. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

Γ should be defined as the family of open γ-covers of X: the cover is infinite and every x∈X belongs to all but finitely many of its members. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
T should be defined as the family of open τ-covers of X. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

A τ-cover should be unpacked as a large cover, meaning each x∈X belongs to infinitely many members, together with the comparability condition that for every x,y∈X either {U:x∈U and y∉U} is finite or {U:y∈U and x∉U} is finite. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

S1(Ω, T) should be expanded: for every sequence of ω-covers of X, one chooses a single member from each cover so that the chosen family is a τ-cover. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

Ufin(O, Γ) should be expanded: only sequences of open covers with no finite subcover are considered, and one chooses finite subfamilies whose unions form a γ-cover. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

For full paper-faithfulness, one may note the ambient convention that for sets of reals the open covers under discussion may be assumed countable. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))

The word "imply" should be understood as a ZFC implication between properties of every such X, not merely a consistency statement. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
refined_question: For a set of real numbers X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers of X (every finite F⊆X is contained in some member of the cover), Γ the family of open γ-covers of X (the cover is infinite and each x∈X belongs to all but finitely many members), and T the family of open τ-covers of X, where covers are understood to be nontrivial (X is not itself a member of the cover), a large cover is one in which each x∈X belongs to infinitely many members, and a τ-cover is a large cover 𝒰 such that for every x,y∈X either {U∈𝒰:x∈U and y∉U} is finite or {U∈𝒰:y∈U and x∉U} is finite. Must every set of reals X satisfying S1(Ω, T)—that is, for every sequence (𝒰_n)n∈ℕ of members of Ω there exist U_n∈𝒰_n such that {U_n:n∈ℕ} is a τ-cover of X—also satisfy Ufin(O, Γ)—that is, for every sequence (𝒱_n)n∈ℕ of open covers of X with no finite subcover there exist finite families 𝔽_n⊆𝒱_n such that {⋃𝔽_n:n∈ℕ} is a γ-cover of X?
justification: The draft is already aimed at the exact official problem in the paper: Section 7.1 first defines τ-covers and the class T, and then states Problem 7.3 in precisely this form. Section 1 provides the selection-principle notation S1(A, B) and Ufin(A, B), along with O, Ω, and Γ, while the introduction also fixes the chapter’s scope to sets of real numbers and notes that in this setting open covers may be taken countable. So the faithful refinement is not to replace the question, but only to unpack the notation and implicit quantifiers so that the problem becomes stand-alone. ([carmamaths.org](https://carmamaths.org/jon/Preprints/Books/Open%20Probs%20in%20Top/open2.pdf))
